Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split this between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split the £20,000 between cash, stocks and shares, innovative finance and Lifetime ISAs. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000 within that total. Unused allowance does not carry forward.

The cash ISA cap of £12,000 for under-65s starts from 6 April 2027, so it doesn't apply in 2026/27. You can read more in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The guide I found says adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year. It also says a Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. It does not say whether a 17-year-old can open an ISA with Fernhill Wealth.

I don't know the answer for your daughter's age. Would you like me to escalate this to an adviser?

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

You can open a Lifetime ISA if you're aged 18 to 39. Withdrawals are free of charge in these cases:
- buying a first home costing £450,000 or less, once the account has been open at least 12 months
- from age 60
- if you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live

Any other withdrawal incurs a 25% government charge. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

A Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. The guide does not say anything about age 42 specifically.

Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year. The allowance can be split between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA, subject to the Lifetime ISA's own limit of £4,000. More detail is in the ISAs guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

From 6 April 2027, our ISA guide lists these changes:

- **Cash ISA cap:** Investors under 65 can pay in up to £12,000 a tax year. The overall £20,000 allowance doesn't change, so the remainder can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- **Transfers:** You can no longer transfer from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs.
- **Interest charge:** A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- **Existing money:** Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The guide doesn't say what you should do about your own ISAs. Please raise that with your adviser.

The £12,000 cash ISA cap is for investors under 65, so it doesn't apply to you at 70. From 6 April 2027, investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit. Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

Another change from the same date is that transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own money. If you want advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, transfers between cash ISAs should take no longer than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days. Re-registering holdings in specie can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

The new provider starts the transfer, so use their transfer process rather than withdrawing the money. We don't charge for transfers in or out. We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

More detail is in the ISA guide at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. You can replace money you withdraw during a tax year in that same tax year, and it won't use more of your allowance.

More detail is in our ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in effect. A surviving spouse or civil partner is entitled to an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is in addition to their own allowance. It applies whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

Your ISA also stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. The documents don't cover how this would work in your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser.

The annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year goes over that, an annual allowance charge is normally due. The total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **High earners:** The allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** This is £10,000. It applies to further defined contribution contributions once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own pension. An adviser can help with that.

The documents say that once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions. They do not say directly whether you can still pay in.

The documents don't cover your own circumstances, so please raise that with your adviser. The source is https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Up to 25% of a pension can normally be taken tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above the allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't advise on how much you should take or when. If you want advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can start drawing from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise and offer to book a free guidance appointment for you. That applies unless you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

I can't advise on which option suits you. For that, an adviser would need to help.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest.

The documents don't say what the rule is for transfer values of £30,000 or less. Please raise that with an adviser.

Under our pensions guide, the rules change on 6 April 2027. From that date, most unused pension funds and death benefits will count towards the value of your estate for inheritance tax.

These are exempt:
- Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner.
- Benefits passing to a registered charity.

Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Income tax is a separate matter. If you die before 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

I can't say how this applies to your own circumstances. For that, please speak to an adviser. Our financial planning service covers inheritance tax and estate planning.

For your own situation, please raise it with your adviser. The source is https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. Our pensions guide says unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

For context, the annual allowance is £60,000. For high earners it tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. The documents don't say how much you could carry forward in your own case. Please raise that with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

A full financial plan costs £2,400, plus VAT where it applies. It covers a review of your whole financial position, a written plan with recommendations, and a meeting to go through it.

One-off advice on a single topic costs £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. An example is how to use allowances before the end of the tax year. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

Otherwise we acknowledge your complaint in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it. More details: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

If you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service free of charge. For a general investment account or ISA:

- **Cash already available:** we pay within five working days of your instruction.
- **Holdings have to be sold first:** sales normally settle within two working days of dealing. We then pay within five working days of settlement.

Pension withdrawals depend on your age and the type of pension, and tax may be payable. The Pensions page explains the options.

Valuation reports are issued quarterly. They're published to the client portal within 15 working days of the end of March, June, September and December.

You can also ask your adviser's team for a valuation as at any date. It is normally available within two working days.

A change of the bank account we pay withdrawals to needs a signed instruction and a recent statement for the new account showing your name. We confirm the change with you by telephone on the number we hold before it takes effect.

Withdrawals are paid only to a bank account in your name that we have verified in this way. The information I have does not say how to send the instruction and statement to us, so please ask your adviser.

Yes. All documents are published to the portal. You can also get paper copies by post at no extra charge. To arrange this, ask your adviser's team.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

Yes. Interest is paid on cash balances at the rates shown on the portal. We keep a margin of 0.25% a year between the rate we receive and the rate we pay. Your client agreement discloses this.

Interest on cash outside an ISA or pension is taxable. It is reported on your annual consolidated tax certificate. From 6 April 2027 a charge will also apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares ISA. The ISA guide explains this.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Regular income is paid on the 25th of the month to your verified bank account. You can take it monthly, quarterly or annually from a general investment account or ISA.

More detail is on the Cash, income payments and dealing page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The smallest monthly direct debit you can set up is £250. Regular contributions are invested in line with your agreed portfolio on the next dealing day after we receive them.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Fund sales are placed at the fund's next valuation point and settle within four working days. Money from a sale can be paid out once settlement has taken place. For a sale on Monday, settlement would therefore be within four working days of the sale.

If you want the money withdrawn, the documents say a withdrawal is paid within five working days of settlement when holdings had to be sold first. They don't give an exact date for your sale. More detail is on the Cash and dealing page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The annual exempt amount for capital gains tax is £3,000. It applies to gains on investments sold in a general investment account. Gains above that on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income.

Losses can be set against gains in the same year, or carried forward if reported to HMRC. Income and gains within an ISA or pension are free of UK income tax and capital gains tax.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Dividends are tax-free within the dividend allowance of £500 a year. Above the allowance, dividends are taxed at 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers, 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers and 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Fernhill publishes the consolidated tax certificate to the client portal by the end of May each year. It shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

We do not complete tax returns. Your adviser can introduce you to an accountant if you need one.

We provide a consolidated tax certificate, published to the portal by the end of May each year, showing dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year. We also provide a capital gains report, showing realised gains and losses and the figures needed for the capital gains pages of a tax return.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

A Bed and ISA means selling holdings in a general investment account and buying them back within an ISA. It uses your ISA allowance and may realise a capital gain.

There is no dealing charge for a Bed and ISA on our model portfolios. The documents don't say whether any other costs apply, or what happens outside model portfolios. Please ask your adviser about those.

More information: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Pension transfers typically take four to eight weeks. The receiving provider starts the transfer. Their scheme carries out the checks required by the pension transfer regulations. If those checks raise an amber flag, it may require you to take guidance from MoneyHelper.

We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The new provider starts the transfer. Once we receive their request, we act on it.

You should use the new provider's transfer process, not withdraw the money yourself. That way the ISA keeps its tax status. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

HMRC guidelines say ISA transfers should complete within 30 calendar days. For transfers between cash ISAs, the guideline is 15 working days. Re-registering holdings in specie can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

Yes. Your documents stay available in the portal for seven years after the account closes. You can ask for paper copies at any time at no charge.

More details are on the closing or transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

**Discretionary management:** You agree an investment mandate and risk level with us. Our investment managers then make the day-to-day decisions within that mandate.

**Advisory management:** We recommend changes, and you decide whether to make each one.

Which one suits you depends on how involved you want to be in individual decisions. Your adviser will discuss both with you, and the choice is recorded in your suitability report. For corporate actions such as rights issues, we handle them for you under a discretionary mandate. Under an advisory mandate, we write to you with the options.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Portfolios are managed to one of seven risk profiles. Profile 1 is the lowest risk, mainly cash and short-dated bonds. Profile 7 is the highest risk, almost entirely equities.

You agree your profile with your adviser. This uses a questionnaire and a conversation about your capacity for loss. It is reviewed at every annual review.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

For a discretionary portfolio, yes. If its value falls by 10% or more since the start of a quarterly reporting period, "we tell you by the end of the working day on which it happens, as the rules require."

You also get a quarterly valuation report on the client portal. It is published within 15 working days of each quarter end. Your investment manager can discuss any report with you. The documents don't say how a fall on a non-discretionary portfolio is handled, so please ask your adviser about that.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

No. Your investments are held by our independent custodian through its nominee company, and legal title is registered in the nominee's name. You remain the beneficial owner.

Your holdings are identified to you in the custodian's records. They are kept separate from the firm's and the custodian's own assets under the Financial Conduct Authority's client assets rules. If the firm or the custodian failed and there were a shortfall, the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may cover eligible claims up to £85,000 per person.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Yes. Each risk profile comes in a responsible version. It excludes companies that get more than 10% of their revenue from tobacco, controversial weapons or thermal coal. It also applies our published responsible investment policy when selecting funds.

Fees are the same as for the standard portfolios. These portfolios don't carry a sustainability label under the FCA's Sustainability Disclosure Requirements. The Responsible Investment Policy sets out the exclusion list and how we measure it. You can request it from us or find it on the website: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

I can't advise on whether this option suits you. For that, please speak to an adviser.

Yes, Fernhill Wealth is covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS).

- **Investment business:** If we were unable to meet our obligations, eligible clients could claim up to £85,000 per person.
- **Cash:** Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

The FSCS website has more details. You can also read more at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/about-us/

Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

Separately, if Fernhill Wealth were unable to meet its obligations, eligible clients could claim compensation of up to £85,000 per person for investment business. The documents say details are on the FSCS website. They do not say how this applies to your own circumstances.

We have six offices: Bristol (head office), London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Leeds and Birmingham. Advisers at every office are also available for telephone and video meetings.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Yes. Fernhill Wealth is a trading name of Fernhill Wealth Limited, which is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. You can check our authorisation on the Financial Services Register at register.fca.org.uk.

Fernhill Wealth Limited is registered in England and Wales. Its registered office is Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY.

Fernhill Wealth gives independent advice. We consider products from across the whole market and are not restricted to any provider's range.

You can read more on our financial planning page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

If you both decide to go ahead, we send a client agreement setting out the agreed work and fees before anything is charged. To book, use the Book an Appointment page or call the new client enquiry line on 0808 157 0450.

For a planning meeting, it helps to have recent statements for any pensions, investments, mortgages and insurance policies, and an idea of your income and regular outgoings.

In our financial planning process, the written plan is presented at a second meeting. That meeting is usually three to four weeks after your discovery meeting. The documents give this as a usual timing, not a guarantee.

More detail is on the financial planning page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

Yes. One-off advice is available on a single topic, such as whether to consolidate pensions. It follows the same process on a smaller scale and is confirmed in a suitability report.

One-off advice on a single topic costs £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. More detail is on the Financial planning service page and the Fees and charges page of the Fernhill Wealth website.

You can book a free introductory appointment in two ways. You can use the Book an Appointment page (https://www.fernhillwealth.example/book-an-appointment/), or you can call the new client enquiry line on 0808 157 0450.
